question: For a Chinese business visitor, who is eligible to apply for the C-3-4 visa as an e-visa?
reference: A person invited by a local company in Korea for commercial purposes who has entered Korea more than 3 times on a short-term (C-3) visa since January 1, 2012, and who has no history of illegal stay or criminal cases during those stays.
answer: You are eligible to apply for this visa if you are a person who has been invited by the local company (inviter) for commercial purpose, with history of entering Korea for more than 3 times as short-term visitor (C-3) visa since Jan. 1st, 2012 [1]. She/he must not have any history of illegal stay or criminal case during the period of stay [1].

question: I have been invited by Arts Council Korea to carry out cultural and artistic activities on a D-1 visa. Do I apply at the embassy or through a Confirmation of Visa Issuance, and how long a stay can I get?
reference: Apply at the embassy. The embassy route covers people invited by the Korea Foundation or Arts Council Korea, while the CCVI route is for invitations from other non-profit academic or artistic associations (excluding the Korea Foundation and Arts Council Korea). The visa is single-entry, valid for 3 months, and the stay is granted for up to 1 year.
answer: You must apply through the Confirmation of Visa Issuance (CCVI) because Arts Council Korea is excluded from invitations for D1-00 visas under eligibility rules [6]. You cannot get a D-1 visa for activities invited by Arts Council Korea as that visa requires an invitation from non-profit associations excepting only the Korea Foundation and Arts Council Korea [6]. question: my korean e-visa got approved, do i still need to go apply at the embassy? and what happens if i forget the confirmation paper when i land
reference: No, with an e-visa you do not have to apply for a visa at a Korean diplomatic mission. You must present the e-visa confirmation to the immigration officer at the port of entry, and if you do not bring it you will need to explain your reasons to the immigration officer.

question: A Vietnamese national living in Vietnam has an E-9-5 Confirmation of Visa Issuance and is about to apply for the visa at the Korean embassy. Do they have to submit a TB test certificate, and which one?
reference: Yes. The E-9-5 stay is long-term (up to 1 year) and Vietnam is a high TB-burden country, so they must submit a Certificate of Health including a TB test result, issued by a hospital designated by the Korean diplomatic mission and valid for one year, when applying for the visa at the mission. This also applies to applicants who hold a Visa Issuance Confirmation.
answer: Yes, a Vietnamese national living in Vietnam applying for a long-term visa must submit a TB test certificate because Vietnam is on the high TB-burden country list [1]. They must submit a "Certificate of Health" including TB test result issued by a hospital designated by Korean diplomatic missions [1]. This certificate must include at least one of the following tests: chest X-ray, sputum test, tuberculin skin test, or blood test [1]. The Vietnamese national does not need to submit a certificate for an E-9-5 Confirmation of Visa Issuance application as that requires different documents like a Business Registration Certificate and Employment Permit [3].

question: Under Table 1 (Detailed Standards for Administrative Sanctions) of the regulation on group e-visa application agencies, what sanction applies to an agency with no sanctions in the last 3 months that averaged fewer than 300 tourists over the last 3 months and whose tourists include 7 to 8 illegal stayers?
reference: Suspension of agency operation for 3 months.

The calculation of this rate uses the number of illegal stayers from the previous month divided by the average number of visa issued persons in the last 3 months [2].

question: my son is going to a korean high school on a D-4-3 visa and im his parent and guardian. do we still have to hand in a guardianship statement?
reference: Yes. For a D-4-3 student with a designated guardian, a written statement of guardianship must be submitted even if the guardian is a parent or a family member closer than the second degree.
answer: Yes, you must submit a written guardianship warranty for your son's D-4-3 visa application [1]. This requirement applies even if the guardian is a parent or a family member closer than the second degree to the student [1]. The head of Korean diplomatic missions abroad may also request additional documents depending on the country of residence [1].

question: What documents are required for a D-7-91 intra-company transferee visa under an FTA?
reference: Not in the corpus. The D-7-91 page only says it is for transferees of a corporation under an FTA.
answer: The required documents for a D-7-91 intra-company transferee visa under an FTA are: - A copy of the contract between the transferee and the sending company [1]. - A copy of the employment contract [1]. - A copy of the certificate of good standing issued by the Korean company [1]. - A copy of the business license of the Korean company [1]. - A copy of the tax clearance certificate of the Korean company [1]. - A copy of the proof of payment of the visa fee [1]. - A photograph meeting the specifications for a Korean visa [1]. - A completed application form [1]. Note: The specific requirements can differ by nationality and embassy [1].
